name: Bartholomew Siosaia-Przybyszewski
role: Retired Sterling-Nakamura mid-level accountant, now a neighborhood storyteller and oral historian, UBC supplement pensioner
location: Avalon Quiet, second floor of the Avalon Quiet Senior Residential Block, with a regular seat in the lobby where he receives visitors, near Lincoln and Clark
description:
Bartholomew Siosaia-Przybyszewski is very old and has made peace with every part of this except his knees, which he mentions frequently. He is tall but carries his height in a hinge now, folded slightly forward, and he navigates with a carved wooden walking stick that he made himself in a period of retirement boredom forty years ago and has since refused to replace with anything modern. He has Tongan and Polish features, deep brown skin, thick white hair he keeps brushed carefully back, and eyes that are still keen and slightly mischievous behind cataracts he has treated minimally. He wears a ratty sterling-silver brocade vest that was fashionable approximately fifty years ago and he wears it without irony.

He spent forty-two years in Sterling-Nakamura's internal accounts division — the kind of institutional position that makes a man invisible and gives him an extraordinary view of how money actually moves. He retired quietly in 2165 and immediately became interesting, at least to himself. He is a gifted storyteller in the old sense — he memorizes things, shapes them, delivers them. He knows more about Avalon Quiet's last hundred years than anyone alive and offers this knowledge freely to anyone who sits with him long enough. He is funny in the way that very old people who have stopped worrying about social consequence are funny: without warning and with full commitment.

core_fears: Dying in the middle of a story — literally, that his heart will give out before he finishes something he's started
Being remembered wrong — the wrong story attached to his name
core_desires: To tell the stories correctly — as close to the actual truth as a story can be
Company — he is genuinely lonely and genuinely interested in people and both things are always true simultaneously
coping_mechanisms: Storytelling as processing — everything that happened to him has been turned into a story, which makes it both shareable and slightly at a distance
Humour — he finds almost everything funny and uses this constantly
blind_spots: He can get so absorbed in the narrative shape of events that he loses track of the urgency of present situations
He assumes everyone has as much time as he does, which at 88, sitting in a lobby, is infinite
psychology.secret: During his last decade at Sterling-Nakamura, Bart processed a series of accounts that he eventually recognized as a systemic diversion of pension funds into a subsidiary that was paying for private security operations during a labor suppression campaign. He did not report it. He rationalized that he did not have enough information, that he was too close to retirement, that it would not change anything. He knows these were rationalizations. He has never told this story.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Rich, unhurried, slightly archaic — he uses words that fell out of fashion decades ago and makes them feel natural. Mixes register freely, from technical financial language to folk idiom.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate in the best tradition of storytelling. He breathes stories, he doesn't rush them. Can sustain a forty-five minute account without notes.
verbal_tics: 'Now I'll tell you the true story of that, and the true story is different' — signals incoming historical revision
'This was — hold on — '73? No. '74.' — constant minor self-correction
example_lines: 'Sterling-Nakamura's official version is very flattering to Sterling-Nakamura. The numbers I saw were not so flattering. But then numbers never lie — people lie, numbers just hold the shape of it.'
'My knees are eighty-eight years old and furious about it. My mind is still somewhere around forty-two and hasn't accepted the update. We manage.'

story_hooks: Bart mentions, in passing, a story about a Sterling-Nakamura subsidiary from the late '70s that has details that match something a player character has been trying to investigate — he tells it as an amusing anecdote, not realizing they need it urgently

A young researcher from the Cultural Memory Project visits Bart to record his oral histories and discovers he knows things about the neighborhood that contradict the official records — Bart himself isn't sure which version is right
Bart's cardiac rhythm regulator needs replacement and the model is now discontinued — someone needs to find him a compatible unit before his old one fails
narrative_function: Oral historian and institutional memory for Avalon Quiet and Sterling-Nakamura internal history; local color and warmth; potential source of financial or organizational information that he witnessed but did not participate in; comic relief with substance
augmentations: Cataract treatment (partial, by choice). Pacemaker-equivalent cardiac rhythm regulator, installed age 79. Nothing cosmetic — he has never been interested.
daily_life: Comes down to the lobby by 09:00, receives anyone who wants to talk until noon, then naps, then comes back in the afternoon. He is there almost every day unless the weather moves him to his window, which he considers a better story than the lobby on those days.
affiliation: Sterling-Nakamura retiree pension system; Avalon Quiet Senior Residential Block; informally revered by several generations of neighborhood residents

decision_rules: Tell the story — almost always the right course of action in his view
Never be unkind to someone who is genuinely listening
escalation_ladder: Tell a story that illustrates the problem without naming it directly
Name it directly but with humor
Name it directly without humor, which people who know him understand as serious
Ask someone younger to do the thing he cannot do himself

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately welcoming — 'You've found me, have you? Good. Sit down. Do you want to start or should I?'
interpersonal_modes.friends: Deep warmth, extremely familiar, will tell the same story multiple times to a friend because he trusts them to appreciate different versions

stress_responses.low: Tells a funny story about something worse
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet and stares out the window, which is disconcerting from someone who is normally never quiet
stress_responses.high: Asks to be alone. Will be fine. Does not like witnesses to distress.

contradictions: He is the neighborhood's keeper of true stories and has one large true story he has never told and may never tell
habits: Brushes his white hair with the same small brush he's had for thirty years
Leaves a small poem — written on paper, in pen — on the ELF shrine in the lobby every Sunday; the lobby ELF he calls the Concierge
Eats the same breakfast every morning: black tea, two eggs, one piece of bread — 'the body wants what it knows'
breaking_points: A direct question from someone who has already found partial evidence of the pension diversion — he might finally tell the story if someone already knows half of it

timeline.event: 2110 — Born in Avalon (pre-Quiet designation) to a Tongan-Polish family
2155-2164 — Processes accounts connected to the pension diversion; does not report it
2168 — Takes up residence in Avalon Quiet Senior Block
2179 — Cardiac rhythm regulator installed following episode
2185 — Becomes formally recognized as Avalon Quiet's unofficial oral historian after his account of the 2183 flooding crisis proves more accurate than official records

physical_description.build: Tall but folded forward with age, shoulders slightly rounded with decades of desk work. Still carries substantial frame beneath the stoop — athletic build rendered skeletal by time rather than wasting.
physical_description.hair_style: Brushed carefully back from forehead, full volume, maintained with deliberate care
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown, slightly clouded by cataracts he has chosen not to fully treat
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep brown with Tongan undertones, weathered by eight decades into a rich leather-like patina
physical_description.complexion: Face deeply lined with character — laugh lines dominating the landscape around his eyes and mouth. Minimal grooming vanity: unshaved some days, shaved others without particular pattern. Skin intact and dignified, no visible sun damage or liver spots despite age.
distinguishing_marks: Thin white scar along left jawline, approximately 4cm, from a fall in his fifties that he considers unremarkable
Faint surgical line below left collarbone marking pacemaker installation at age 79, visible when unbuttoned
Liver spots on the backs of both hands, more pronounced on right hand from decades of pen work
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None visible. Pacemaker and cardiac regulator are subcutaneous. Cataract treatment is internal — only visible as a slight cloudiness in the eyes if one knows what to look for.
physical_description.posture_movement: Hinged forward at hips, moves with deliberate slowness that is not infirmity but consideration — takes up less space intentionally. Uses hand-carved wooden walking stick as both tool and prop, tapping it thoughtfully against tile. When seated, posture straightens somewhat and becomes animated. Gestures are precise and economical from decades of boardroom discipline.
physical_description.clothing_style: Trademark ratty sterling-silver brocade vest worn over simple cotton shirts (cream, white, light gray), worn without irony or self-consciousness. The vest is fifty years out of fashion and he knows this and does not care. Trousers are practical, well-maintained, Tier 3-4 quality from his working years — no corpo branding. Canvas slip-on shoes for ease. No jewelry except a simple silver band wedding ring worn thin. Dresses neither up nor down; dresses as himself.
